title: buildclamp attestation predicate v1
description: The predicate body of an in-toto Statement v1 produced by buildclamp. It states that an artefact with a given content hash was built while a given policy and a given report were in effect, and which enforcement tier actually applied on the build host. It does NOT state that the enforcement was correct, that the policy was a good one, or that the build was reproducible. This file is normative; the $id is an identifier and is never fetched.

format_version.description: 1 or 2. Version 2 adds `waivers` and makes it required reading (a waived build is not fully enforced). A verifier accepts both; it refuses a version-1 statement after the stated sunset (2028-01-01), because a format nobody re-issues is a format nobody audits.

artefact_name.description: A name, never a path: a path is meaningless on the machine that verifies this.

policy_sha256.description: Two builds under 'the same policy' that hash differently were not under the same policy.

policy_signature_verified.description: Whether every distributed policy layer verified against the repository's committed trust root — the policy's AUTHORITY (who was allowed to write it), which policy_sha256 alone cannot establish. False when no trust root is in use or a layer was unsigned. Optional and additive: a v1 document written before this field is read with it false.

policy_signer_key_id.description: The trust-root key id(s) that signed the distributed layers, when any did; several are joined by commas across a rotation window or multiple layers. Absent when nothing was verified.

enforcement_summary.description: The WEAKEST tier seen for each capability across every unit in the run. Weakest, not last or strongest: one advisory unit among two hundred enforced is the single most useful thing this document can tell a reader.

operator_overrides.description: Enforcement an operator switched off or down. Non-empty means is_fully_enforced() is false, whatever the tiers say: a switched-off mechanism leaves behind either nothing or a weaker one still reporting 'enforced:'.

waivers.description: Gates a human waived with break-glass: exceptions a unit actually exercised. Added in format version 2. A non-empty array means the build was let through by an override and is NOT fully enforced, whatever the tiers say. Optional and omitted when empty, so a version-1 document has none.

enforcementProfile.description: Every optional enforcement flag and its state. Without this a run with both hardenings off produces a statement whose every tier says 'enforced:' — truthfully, about the capabilities that were held — and a reader concludes 'fully enforced' about a build where a build script could read every credential file on the host and no proc-macro was held at all.

read_deny.description: `withhold-secret-reads`. False means every unit could read every path on the host.

read_deny_ruleset_sha256.description: Which deny-list was in force. The list changes between releases, so 'read_deny was on' does not by itself say which paths were withheld. Absent when read_deny is false.

compile_units_held.description: `hold-compile-units`. False means proc-macro expansion ran unheld — the half of the threat a build-script-only tool misses entirely.

net_destinations_recorded_only.description: Always true, and recorded anyway: a reader must not have to know this project's documentation to find out that a destination list is not a control.

landlock_abi_used.description: The ABI the run used, or absent where Landlock was unavailable. ABI is a tier dimension: landlock-v1 cannot restrict truncation.

disable_overrides.description: Repeated from operator_overrides so this object stands alone: a consumer reading only the profile must not be able to conclude 'everything on' about a run somebody had switched down.

scope.description: What was NOT held, in words. Distinct from enforcement_profile, which is a list of switches; this is the sentence somebody reads. An empty list is a claim that there were no gaps, not the absence of a claim.
